<!-- No citations are required in the article lead per [[MOS:LEADCITE]], as long as the content is cited in the article body, as it should be. Do not add missing-citation tags like {{cn}} to the lead. If necessary, {{not verified in body}} can be used, or the content removed. -->

In January 2022, [[15 (software engineer)|15]]&mdash;the pseudonymous [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) artificial intelligence researcher and creator of the non-commercial [[generative artificial intelligence]] [[voice synthesis]] research project [[15.ai]]&mdash;discovered that the [[blockchain]]-based technology company '''Voiceverse''' had [[plagiarism|plagiarized]] from their platform. Voiceverse marketed itself as a service that offered [[audio deepfake|AI voice cloning technology]] that could be purchased and traded as [[non-fungible token]]s (NFTs).

Amid heightened controversy over NFTs in the gaming industry, voice actor [[Troy Baker]] (who has been described as one of the most famous [[Voice acting#Voice acting in video games|voice actors in video games]]) announced his partnership with Voiceverse on January 14, 2022, triggering immediate backlash over concerns about the [[Non-fungible token#Environmental concerns|environmental impact of NFTs]], [[Non-fungible token#Plagiarism and fraud|potential for fraud]], [[Video game monetization#Criticism|predatory monetization in video games]], and the potential of [[technological unemployment|AI displacing jobs for human voice actors]]. Later that same day, 15 revealed through server logs that Voiceverse had generated voice lines using 15.ai, pitch-shifted the audio to make them unrecognizable, and [[false advertising|falsely marketed]] the samples as their own technology before selling them as NFTs. Within an hour of being confronted with evidence, Voiceverse confessed and stated that their marketing team had used 15.ai without proper attribution while rushing to create a [[technology demo]] to coincide with Baker's partnership announcement, further exacerbating the already negative reception to the original announcement. In response, 15 replied "[[Go fuck yourself]]"; the interaction went [[viral phenomenon|viral]] and garnered a large amount of support for the developer. News publications universally characterized this incident as Voiceverse having [[theft|stolen]] from 15.ai.

The next day, Baker appeared on a [[podcast]] and stated that his motivation had been to help independent creators who were unable to afford professional voice actors. Following continued backlash and the plagiarism revelation, Baker ended his partnership with Voiceverse on January 31, 2022. Subsequently, the incident was documented in multiple [[AI ethics]] databases, criticisms of predatory monetization in video games, and [[retrospective]]s as one of the earliest instances of plagiarism and theft stemming from artificial intelligence during the [[AI boom]]. After its parent company LOVO, Inc. filed for [[Chapter 7 bankruptcy]], Voiceverse shut down and ceased all operations on May 27, 2026.

=== Voiceverse ===
Voiceverse is a [[blockchain]]-based startup founded by the [[Bored Ape Yacht Club]]<ref name="McKean-2022">{{cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/story/tech/gaming/2022/01/14/actor-troy-baker-endorses-nft-voice-ai/81408726007/|title=Actor Troy Baker endorses NFT voice AI that aims to replace actors|first=Kirk|last=McKean|website=[[USA Today]]|date=January 14, 2022|access-date=October 5, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250730094536/https://ftw.usatoday.com/story/tech/gaming/2022/01/14/actor-troy-baker-endorses-nft-voice-ai/81408726007/|archive-date=July 30, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> that marketed itself as offering AI voice cloning technology in the form of [[NFT]]s.<ref name="Makuch-2022"/> Prior to the announcement of their partnership with Baker, Voiceverse had partnered with LOVO, Inc., an AI voice platform that, according to LOVO, could generate human-like voices.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> Voiceverse stated that any user who purchases a voice NFT would have unlimited and perpetual access to the voice model,<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> which could be used to create content such as [[audiobook]]s, [[YouTube video]]s, [[podcast]]s, e-learning materials, in-game [[voice chat]], and [[Zoom call]]s.<ref name="Phillips-14"/><ref name="Makuch-2022">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/troy-baker-announces-nft-project-for-his-voice-responds-to-criticisms/1100-6499648/|title=Troy Baker Announces NFT Project For His Voice, Responds To Criticisms|website=[[GameSpot]]|first=Eddie|last=Makuch|date=January 14, 2022|access-date=October 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220114155254/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/troy-baker-announces-nft-project-for-his-voice-responds-to-criticisms/1100-6499648/|archive-date=January 14, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Voiceverse promised that buyers would "OWN ''[[sic|[sic]]]'' all of the [[intellectual property|IP]]" of content they created using these voices.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> Voiceverse's roadmap included plans to release 8,888 initial voice NFTs, a feature to add emotions to existing voices, and the ability for users to mint their own voices as NFTs. Prior to Baker's partnership, Voiceverse had also partnered with voice actors [[Charlet Chung]], who voices [[D.Va]] in ''[[Overwatch]]'',<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> and [[Andy Milonakis]] of ''[[The Andy Milonakis Show]]''.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/><ref name="Makuch-2022"/>

=== 15.ai ===
{{Main|15.ai|15 (software engineer)}}
[[File:15chill.png|thumb|15's [[ponysona]] was the mascot of the [[15.ai]] website]]
[[15.ai]] is a free web application launched in 2020 that uses [[artificial intelligence]] to generate [[text-to-speech]] voices of fictional characters from [[popular media]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Ruppert |first=Liana |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Make Portal's GLaDOS And Other Beloved Characters Say The Weirdest Things With This App |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/gamer-culture/2021/01/18/make-portals-glados-and-other-beloved-characters-say-the-weirdest-things |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118175543/https://www.gameinformer.com/gamer-culture/2021/01/18/make-portals-glados-and-other-beloved-characters-say-the-weirdest-things |archive-date=January 18, 2021 |access-date=October 5, 2025 |magazine=[[Game Informer]]|url-status=live}}</ref> Created by a [[pseudonym]]ous artificial intelligence researcher known as [[15 (software engineer)|15]], who began developing the technology as a [[freshman]] during their undergraduate research at [[MIT]], it was an early example of an application of [[generative artificial intelligence]] during the initial stages of the [[AI boom]]. The platform showed that [[deep neural networks]] could generate emotionally expressive speech with only 15 seconds of speech; the name "15.ai" references the creator's statement that a voice can be convincingly cloned with just 15 seconds of audio, as opposed to the tens of hours of data previously required. 15.ai became an [[Internet phenomenon]] in early 2021 when content utilizing it went viral on [[social media]] and quickly gained widespread use among various [[fandom|Internet fandom]]s. 15 has emphasized that it remain free and non-commercial; it only requires users to give proper credit when using the service for content creation.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Abisola |first=Shojobi |date=January 3, 2025 |title=The MIT Project That Paved Way For Modern Voice AI | url=https://independent.ng/the-mit-project-that-paved-way-for-modern-voice-ai/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|url-status=live | access-date=October 5, 2025|newspaper=[[Independent Nigeria|Independent]]|archive-date=February 27, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250227050616/https://independent.ng/the-mit-project-that-paved-way-for-modern-voice-ai/ }}</ref>

=== NFTs in the video game industry ===
{{Main|Non-fungible token#Issues and criticisms}}
By early 2022, NFTs had become highly controversial within the gaming industry.<ref name="McKean-2022"/> Critics raised concerns about their environmental impact due to the significant energy consumption of blockchain technology.<ref name="McKean-2022"/> In addition, the prevalence of scams, fraud, and potential [[money laundering]] associated with NFT sales, as well as fears that NFTs were a new form of [[Video game monetization#Criticism|predatory monetization]] following the increasing frequency of [[loot boxes]], caused vocal pushback from the gaming community.<ref name="McKean-2022"/> Several major gaming companies had begun exploring NFT integration into their products, though fan backlash had already forced some projects to be cancelled.<ref name="Bankhurst-2022">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/troy-baker-nft-voiceverse-pulls-out|title=Voice Actor Troy Baker Pulls Out of NFT Partnership [Update]|date=January 14, 2022|access-date=October 5, 2025|website=[[IGN]]|first=Adam|last=Bankhurst|editor-first=Matt|editor-last=Purslow|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250828090132/https://www.ign.com/articles/troy-baker-nft-voiceverse-pulls-out|archive-date=August 28, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 16, 2021,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/12/16/22840488/stalker-2-nft-metahuman-gsc-web3-canceled|title=S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 will no longer have NFTs after fan outcry|first=Jay|last=Peters|website=[[The Verge]]|date=December 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251001203045/https://www.theverge.com/2021/12/16/22840488/stalker-2-nft-metahuman-gsc-web3-canceled|archive-date=October 1, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> the developers of ''[[S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chernobyl]]'' announced that they would be including NFTs in the game, but cancelled within an hour of the announcement due to immediate universal backlash.<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/><ref name="Peters-2022"/> Simultaneously, the rise of AI voice technology raised concerns among voice actors about potential job displacement and the devaluation of their work amidst the voice acting industry's ongoing struggles for better compensation and working conditions.<ref name="McKean-2022"/><ref name="Brown-2022">{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/troy-baker-criticised-for-supporting-company-that-makes-ai-voice-nfts-3137906|website=[[NME]]|first=Andy|last=Brown|date=January 14, 2022|access-date=October 5, 2025|title=Troy Baker criticised for supporting company that makes AI "voice NFTs"|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007162924/https://www.nme.com/news/troy-baker-criticised-for-supporting-company-that-makes-ai-voice-nfts-3137906|archive-date=October 7, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="McWhertor-2022"/>

== Partnership announcement and backlash ==
{{Tweet
|image         = Troy Baker SDCC 2019 (48378614692) (cropped).jpg
|name          = [[Troy Baker]]
|username      = TroyBakerVA
|width         = 350px
|date          = January 14, 2022, 1:02 a.m.
|text          = I'm partnering with @VoiceverseNFT to explore ways where together we might bring new tools to new creators to make new things, and allow everyone a chance to own & invest in the IP's they create.
We all have a story to tell.
You can hate.
Or you can create.
What'll it be?
|reference     = <ref name="Brown-2022"/>
}}
On January 14, 2022, 1:02{{nbsp}}a.m. [[Eastern Standard Time|EST]], Baker announced on [[Twitter]] that he was partnering with Voiceverse "to explore ways where together we might bring new tools to new creators to make new things, and allow everyone a chance to own & invest in the IP's they create." The announcement concluded with the statement "You can hate. Or you can create."<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/><ref name="Brown-2022"/> Baker's specific role with Voiceverse remained unclear at the time of the announcement.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/>

[[File:Chubbiverse_promotional_video.webm|thumb|left|upright=0.75|A Chubbiverse [[promo video]] posted by Voiceverse. Server logs later showed that the voices were actually generated using [[15.ai]] and had been distorted to sound unrecognizable.]]
Along with Baker's announcement, Voiceverse promoted their supposed voice AI technology on Twitter by posting animated videos that featured a cat character created by NFT firm '''{{visanc|Chubbiverse}}'''.<ref name="Phillips-17">{{cite web |last=Phillips |first=Tom |date=January 17, 2022 |title=Troy Baker-backed NFT firm admits using voice lines taken from another service without permission |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2022-01-17-troy-baker-backed-nft-firm-admits-using-voice-lines-taken-from-another-service-without-permission |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117164033/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2022-01-17-troy-baker-backed-nft-firm-admits-using-voice-lines-taken-from-another-service-without-permission |archive-date=January 17, 2022 |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref><ref name="Innes-2022">{{cite web |last=Innes |first=Ruby |date=January 18, 2022 |title=Voiceverse Is The Latest NFT Company Caught Using Someone Else's Content |url=https://www.kotaku.com.au/2022/01/voiceverse-caught-using-someone-elses-content/ |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[Kotaku Australia]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240726140924/https://www.kotaku.com.au/2022/01/voiceverse-caught-using-someone-elses-content/|archive-date=July 26, 2024|url-status=usurped}}</ref> The videos concluded with text that read "The Voice Powered By Voiceverse"; Voiceverse stated on Twitter that the voices in the animations had been generated using their own AI voice synthesis technology and presented the videos as a [[technology demonstration]] of their voice NFT capabilities.<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Innes-2022"/>

The announcement provoked immediate and widespread backlash from the gaming community.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> Baker's tweet received thousands of replies and [[Tweet (social media)#Retweets|quote retweets]] (the vast majority of which were negative),<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> far more than the number of [[upvote|likes]];<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/> Michael McWhertor of ''Polygon'' described it as a "textbook example of being [[ratioed]]" and commented that reactions had been amplified by the final part of Baker's announcement.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> Michael Beckwith of ''[[Metro (UK)|Metro]]'' called Baker's approach "bizarrely aggressive".<ref name="Beckwith-2022"/>

Later that day, Baker responded to the backlash by apologizing for his choice of words.<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/> He said he appreciated people's thoughts and acknowledged that the "hate/create part might have been a bit antagonistic," calling it a "bad attempt to bring levity".<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/> Despite the apology, Baker and his fellow voice actors did not distance themselves from Voiceverse at this point.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> At the same time, Voiceverse attempted to address the criticisms, stating that they were working to move to more environmentally friendly blockchain technology and that voice actors would receive royalties from NFT sales, with actors benefiting from any increase in NFT value.<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/>

On December 13, 2021, amidst the increasingly negative reactions toward NFTs among the general public, the creator of [[15.ai]] (known pseudonymously as [[15 (software engineer)|15]]) announced that they had "no interest in incorporating [[NFT]]s into any aspect of [their] work."<ref name="Innes-2022"/><ref name="Wright-2022"/><ref name="Lawrence-2022"/>

On January 14, 2022, 11:17{{nbsp}}a.m. [[Eastern Standard Time|EST]] (10 hours after Baker's initial announcement),<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1482024112700723204|user=fifteenai|title=Sounds like a scam}}</ref> 15 commented on the Voiceverse venture, stating that it "sounds like a [[scam]]".<ref name="W-K">{{cite web |last=Wakelin-King |first=Edith |date=January 15, 2022|title=Troy Baker angers the internet with NFT partnership|url=https://checkpointgaming.net/news/2022/01/troy-baker-angers-the-internet-with-nft-partnership/|access-date=February 28, 2025|website=Checkpoint Gaming|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212033149/https://checkpointgaming.net/news/2022/01/troy-baker-angers-the-internet-with-nft-partnership/|archive-date=December 12, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> Two hours later, at 1:20{{nbsp}}p.m., 15 explicitly accused Voiceverse of "actively attempting to appropriate [15's] work for [Voiceverse's] own benefit."<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Innes-2022"/><ref name="Wright-2022">{{cite web |last=Wright |first=Steve |date=January 17, 2022 |title=Troy Baker-backed NFT company admits to using content without permission |url=https://stevivor.com/news/troy-baker-nft-voiceverse-15-ai/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117231918/https://stevivor.com/news/troy-baker-nft-voiceverse-15-ai/ |archive-date=January 17, 2022 |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=Stevivor}}</ref> 15 provided evidence through server [[log files]] that showed that the voices Voiceverse was claiming credit for had actually been generated by 15.ai.<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Innes-2022"/> The log files, which showed the details of the server [[request–response]]s exactly matching up with those present in Voiceverse's video, proved that Voiceverse had used 15.ai to create the voice samples that they were marketing as their own technology.<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Innes-2022"/> The Chubbiverse promotion videos featured distorted voices of characters{{efn|While sources like ''[[Eurogamer]]''<ref name="Phillips-17"/> and ''[[NME]]''<ref name="Williams-2022"/> mention [[Rainbow Dash]], logs posted by [[15 (software engineer)|15]] showed that the voice of [[Twilight Sparkle]] had also been copied on January 4, 2022.<ref group="tweet" name="Log-1">{{cite tweet |user=fifteenai |number=1482059159092793346 |title=Give proper credit or remove this post.}}</ref><ref group="tweet" name="Log-2">{{cite tweet|user=fifteenai|number=1482076584517455884|title=Unbelievable. They even pitched up the voice to intentionally make it sound unrecognizable from Rainbow Dash's original voice.}}</ref>}} from the animated television series ''[[My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic]]''.<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Williams-2022"/> The voice lines had then been sold as NFTs,<ref name="Phillips-17"/> a violation of 15.ai's [[terms of service]], which explicitly prohibited commercial use and required proper attribution.<ref name="Innes-2022"/>

{{tweet
|image         = 
|name          = Voiceverse
|username      = VoiceverseNFT
|width         = 350px
|date          = January 14, 2022, 2:09 p.m.
|text          = Hey @fifteenai we are extremely sorry about this. The voice was indeed taken from your platform, which our marketing team used without giving proper credit. Chubbiverse team has no knowledge of this. We will make sure this never happens again.
|reference     = <ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Innes-2022"/><ref name="Wright-2022"/>
}}
Voiceverse initially responded sarcastically before deleting that response.<ref name="Wright-2022"/><ref name="Phillips-17"/> At 2:09{{nbsp}}p.m. EST, Voiceverse wrote in an apology to 15: "We are extremely sorry about this. The voice was indeed taken from your platform, which our marketing team used without giving proper credit. Chubbiverse team has no knowledge of this. We will make sure this never happens again."<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Innes-2022"/><ref name="Wright-2022"/> In their [[Discord]] server, Voiceverse further stated that their marketing team had been in such a rush to create a partnership [[technology demo]] that they resorted to using 15.ai without waiting for their own voice technology to be ready.<ref name="Shazoo-2022"/>

In response, at 3:34{{nbsp}}p.m. EST, 15 tweeted "Go fuck yourself";<ref name="Phillips-17"/><ref name="Williams-2022"/><ref name="Groth-Anderson-2022"/> the interaction went [[viral phenomenon|viral]], garnering widespread support for 15.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Temitope |first=Yusuf |date=December 10, 2024 |title=15.ai Creator reveals journey from MIT Project to internet phenomenon |url=https://guardian.ng/technology/15-ai-creator-reveals-journey-from-mit-project-to-internet-phenomenon/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=October 5, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241228152312/https://guardian.ng/technology/15-ai-creator-reveals-journey-from-mit-project-to-internet-phenomenon/ |archive-date=December 28, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> In a subsequent statement, the creator expressed being "extremely depressed" by the incident and wrote: "Not only because my work was stolen and used for profit, but also because of this scandal, the entire field of [[vocal synthesis]] is now being misrepresented by [[charlatan]]s who are only in it for the money."<ref name="Sonali-2022"/><ref name="Beckwith-2022">{{cite web |last=Beckwith |first=Michael |date=January 17, 2022 |title=NFT firm Voiceverse admits it stole work after announcing Troy Baker deal |url=https://metro.co.uk/2022/01/17/nft-firm-voiceverse-stole-work-after-announcing-troy-baker-deal-15934440/ |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[Metro (UK)|Metro]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117180225/https://metro.co.uk/2022/01/17/nft-firm-voiceverse-stole-work-after-announcing-troy-baker-deal-15934440/|archive-date=January 17, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Voiceverse subsequently deleted the incriminating tweet, but Twitter users had already saved and reshared the video.<ref name="Innes-2022"/><ref name="Williams-2022"/>

Critics of Voiceverse pointed out the irony of selling ownership rights to AI voices when they themselves had stolen 15.ai's technology.]]

According to ''Eurogamer'', reactions to Baker's initial partnership announcement were universally negative.<ref name="Phillips-14"/><ref name="Phillips-17"/> Critics raised multiple concerns, including the potential [[Non-fungible token#Environmental concerns|environmental impact of NFT sales]] due to [[Blockchain#Energy consumption concerns|blockchain energy consumption]],<ref name="McWhertor-2022"/> fears that [[deep learning speech synthesis|AI-driven voice technology]] would automate and eliminate the need for actual human voice actors and [[Technological unemployment|jeopardize voice acting jobs]],<ref name="Brown-2022"/><ref name="McKean-2022"/> warnings that the technology could devalue voice actors' work and undercut prospective actors,<ref name="McKean-2022"/> and concerns about [[Non-fungible token#Plagiarism and fraud|scams and art theft associated with NFTs]].<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/> At the same time, fans also accused Baker of abandoning a 2017 music [[crowdfunding]] project and never providing refunds to those who donated.<ref name="Murray-2022"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thegamer.com/troy-baker-crowdfunding-refund-window-to-the-abbey/|title=Troy Baker Allegedly Abandoned Music Crowdfunding Project Without Sending Items Out|first=Rhiannon|last=Bevan|date=January 15, 2022|access-date=October 7, 2025|website=[[TheGamer]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115140222/https://www.thegamer.com/troy-baker-crowdfunding-refund-window-to-the-abbey/|archive-date=January 15, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

The plagiarism revelation immediately exacerbated the already-negative reception. Less than an hour after 15's accusation, [[YouTuber]]s SkillUp and [[Yong Yea]] both reported that by plagiarizing 15.ai's work, Voiceverse had committed theft and fraud.<ref name="Kuchkanov-2022"/><ref name="Martinů-2022"/><ref group="video">{{cite web|first=Yong|last=Yea|author-link=Yong Yea|title=Troy Baker Faces Mass Backlash For Supporting Shady AI Voice NFTs With Company That Has Stolen Work|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kVaBVE5gj54&t=954s|website=[[YouTube]]| date=January 14, 2022 |access-date=March 23, 2025|quote="This isn't just one of those things [Voiceverse] can go 'Whoopsies!' on. [They] plagiarized somebody else's work and used that as a means to falsely market the quality of [their] own products, by using somebody else's higher quality voice AI to promote [Voiceverse] for [their] own benefit."|time=15:54–16:13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241220161229/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kVaBVE5gj54|archive-date=December 20, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>{{rp|15:54–16:13}}

== Aftermath ==
=== Baker's apology and separation ===
{{Multiple image
| image1            = Alanah_Pearce,_GDCA_2024_(cropped).jpg
| image2            = Mike_bithell_GDC_Europe_2013_cropped.jpg
| image3            = Austin_Wintory,_GDC_2024_(D3_KT2_3297)_(cropped).jpg
| total_width       = 450
| caption_align     = center
| caption1          = [[Alanah Pearce]]
| caption2          = [[Mike Bithell]]
| caption3          = [[Austin Wintory]]
}}
On January 15, the day after the plagiarism revelation, Baker appeared on episode 90 of the ''[[Play, Watch, Listen]]'' podcast, which he co-hosts with [[Alanah Pearce]], [[Mike Bithell]], and [[Austin Wintory]]. In the episode, "Talking to Troy Baker About His NFT Tweet," Baker stated that his primary motivation for the partnership was to help independent creators access resources they otherwise could not afford. He said: "while I understood that an NFT was a component to this, that's not what I got involved with." Baker said he envisioned a scenario where "if some independent game maker wants to have me in their game and they can't afford me and they can do that now, great." Responding to concerns that the technology could put voice actors out of work, Baker said: "if the only reason why I don't do something to help somebody out is because it may hurt me, that's a fucked up reason to not do the right thing." He acknowledged that his announcement had been "just a fucking bad look" and apologized again; he also said that he had told Voiceverse he did not know what would happen with the partnership moving forward.<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/>

On January 31, over two weeks after his initial announcement, Baker announced that he would no longer partner with Voiceverse and thanked fans for their "feedback and patience".<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/><ref name="Peters-2022"/><ref name="McWhertor-2022"/><ref name="Murray-2022">{{cite web|url=https://www.thegamer.com/troy-baker-cancels-nft-voiceverse/|title=Troy Baker Decides Against NFT Partnership, Apologizes To Haters|first=Sean|last=Murray|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=October 5, 2025|website=[[TheGamer]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131161327/https://www.thegamer.com/troy-baker-cancels-nft-voiceverse/|archive-date=January 31, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> He reiterated his apology from earlier in the month: "Intentions aside, I've heard you and apologize for accusing anyone of 'hating' just by simply disagreeing with me."<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/><ref name="Peters-2022"/><ref name="McWhertor-2022"/><ref name="Murray-2022"/> Voiceverse stated that the decision was reached as a "mutual agreement" between the two parties and stated that they would "double-down our resources and efforts to execute on our roadmap, further our vision as the voice of [[Web3|Web3.0]], and strengthen our community as well as the broader NFT ecosystem."<ref name="Bankhurst-2022"/>

=== ''Lehrman & Sage v. LOVO, Inc.'' ===
In April 2021, '''{{visanc|LOVO, Inc.}}''' (the parent company of Voiceverse) had written in their company blog post that "[15.ai] are LOVO's competition because we do all of that as well, but none of us are real threats to each other, yet."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lovo.ai/post/the-road-to-general-intelligence-in-synthetic-speech-part-1|title=The Road to General Intelligence in Synthetic Speech (Part 1)|website=LOVO.ai|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=October 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515020226/https://lovo.ai/post/the-road-to-general-intelligence-in-synthetic-speech-part-1|archive-date=May 15, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> On September 25, 2024, a [[class action lawsuit]] was filed by voice actors Paul Skye Lehrman and Linnea Sage against LOVO alleging that the company had illegally copied their voices and had used them without permission. Court documents cited LOVO/Voiceverse's prior plagiarism of 15.ai as part of the case.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/ai-voiceover-company-stole-voices-actors-new-york-lawsuit-claims-2024-05-16/|title=AI voiceover company stole voices of actors, New York lawsuit claims|website=[[Reuters]]|date=May 16, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2025|first=Blake|last=Brittain|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240517190259/https://www.reuters.com/legal/ai-voiceover-company-stole-voices-actors-new-york-lawsuit-claims-2024-05-16/|archive-date=May 17, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="courtcase">{{cite court|litigants=Paul Lehrman and Linnea Sage, et al. v. LOVO, Inc.|vol=|reporter=No. 1:24-cv-03770|opinion=|pinpoint=38|court=S.D.N.Y.|date=2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517052702/https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/legaldocs/dwvkzgknepm/AI%20VOICEOVER%20LAWSUIT%20complaint.pdf|archive-date=October 4, 2025|url-status=live|url=https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/legaldocs/dwvkzgknepm/AI%20VOICEOVER%20LAWSUIT%20complaint.pdf|quote=Separately, VoiceVerse has already been found to have stolen technology from another company. See Ule Lopez, WCCF Tech, "Voiceverse NFT Service Reportedly Uses Stolen Technology from 15ai," (Jan. 16, 2022), https://wccftech.com/voiceverse-nft-service-uses-stolen-technology-from-15ai/.}}</ref> In July 2025, a federal judge in New York dismissed the claims that the artists' voices were subject to federal [[copyright protection]] but permitted the claims of [[breach of contract]], [[unfair business practices]], and separate [[copyright infringement]] claims regarding unauthorized use of their voices in the AI's training data to proceed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cedgzj8z1wjo|title=Federal judge says voice-over artists' AI lawsuit can move forward|website=[[BBC]]|first=Ben|last=Derico|date=July 11, 2025|access-date=November 25, 2025|archive-date=September 30, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930062056/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cedgzj8z1wjo|url-status=live}}</ref>

LOVO, Inc. filed for [[Chapter 7 bankruptcy]] on May 27, 2026, ceasing all operations and permanently shutting down Voiceverse.<ref>{{cite web |first=Annelise|last=Levy|title=Voice Actors’ Suit Against Lovo Paused Amid AI Firm's Bankruptcy|url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/voice-actors-suit-against-lovo-paused-amid-ai-firms-bankruptcy |website=[[Bloomberg Law]]|publisher=Bloomberg|date=May 29, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
The incident was documented by various organizations indexing [[ethics of artificial intelligence|ethics violations in artificial intelligence]] and [[Non-fungible token#Plagiarism and fraud|cryptocurrency]]. Both the [[AI Incident Database]] (AIID) and the [[AI, Algorithmic, and Automation Incidents and Controversies]] (AIAAIC){{efn|which are frequently cited and used by researchers, policymakers, and practitioners studying AI-related incidents and their impacts<ref name="Agarwal-2024">{{cite conference |last1=Agarwal |first1=Avinash |last2=Nene |first2=Manisha |date=October 21, 2024 |title=Advancing Trustworthy AI for Sustainable Development: Recommendations for Standardising AI Incident Reporting |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10772925 |conference=2024 ITU Kaleidoscope: Innovation and Digital Transformation for a Sustainable World |location=New Delhi, India |publisher=IEEE |doi=10.23919/ITUK62727.2024.10772925 |access-date=October 5, 2025 |arxiv=2501.14778}}</ref>}} classified the incident as theft.<ref name="AIAAIC">{{cite web |date=January 2022 |url=https://www.aiaaic.org/aiaaic-repository/ai-algorithmic-and-automation-incidents/voiceverse-nft-voice-theft |title=Voiceverse NFT caught plagiarising voice lines from AI service 15.ai |url-status=live |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[AI, Algorithmic, and Automation Incidents and Controversies]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251004023459/https://www.aiaaic.org/aiaaic-repository/ai-algorithmic-and-automation-incidents/voiceverse-nft-voice-theft |archive-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Sonali-2022">{{cite web |last=Sonali |first=Pednekar |editor-last=Lam |editor-first=Khoa |title=Incident 277: Voices Created Using Publicly Available App Stolen and Resold as NFT without Attribution |url=https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/277/ |website=[[AI Incident Database]] |access-date=October 5, 2025 |date=January 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250113102849/https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/277/ |archive-date=January 13, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Later, the AIAAIC also formally classified the incident as a case of [[plagiarism]].<ref name="AIAAIC"/> The MIT AI Risk Repository catalogued the incident as an example of "economic and cultural devaluation of human effort",<ref name="Sonali-2022"/> and a group of artificial intelligence researchers from [[Penn State University]], [[Arizona State University]], and the [[University of Dhaka]] categorized it as an example of platform governance risk of attribution stripping and commercial exploitation.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Sharma |first1=Tanusree |last2=Krishnagiri |first2=Anish |last3=Dudas |first3=Lili |last4=Adnan |first4=Ahmed |last5=Berisha |first5=Visar |date=25 April 2026 |title=V.O.I.C.E (Voice, Ownership, Identity, Control, Expression): Risk Taxonomy of Synthetic Voice Generation From Empirical Data |eprint=2604.24794 |class=cs.CR}}</ref>

In a [[retrospective]] of the incident on her ''[[Web3 Is Going Just Great]]'' website, writer and crypto skeptic [[Molly White]] wrote that "things were further soured when it was revealed that Voiceverse had stolen work without crediting it from [...] 15.ai." White categorized the incident as theft, a "bad idea", and "shady business".<ref name="White-2022">{{cite web |last=White |first=Molly |date=14 January 2022 |title=Voice actor Troy Baker announces his involvement in "voice NFT" project Voiceverse with an antagonistic tweet, shortly before it's revealed that the project stole work |url=https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=troy-baker-voiceverse-announcement |access-date=October 5, 2025 |website=[[Web3 Is Going Just Great]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240724222800/https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=troy-baker-voiceverse-announcement |archive-date=July 24, 2024 |url-status=live |author-link=Molly White}}</ref> In an article about [[video game monetization]] on the Russian educational platform ''[[:ru:Skillbox|Skillbox]]'', [[video game journalist]] Pavel Khibchenko described the plagiarism incident as an example of [[Non-fungible token#Plagiarism and fraud|fraud in NFTs]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Khibchenko |first=Pavel |date=February 15, 2022 |title=NFT в геймдеве: проблемы регулирования, гнев игроков и поспешные решения разработчиков |url=https://skillbox.ru/media/gamedev/nft-v-geymdeve-problemy-regulirovaniya-gnev-igrokov-i-pospeshnye-resheniya-razrabotchikov/ |access-date=February 28, 2025 |website=[[:ru:Skillbox|Skillbox]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605201046/https://skillbox.ru/media/gamedev/nft-v-geymdeve-problemy-regulirovaniya-gnev-igrokov-i-pospeshnye-resheniya-razrabotchikov/ |archive-date=June 5, 2023 |url-status=live |language=ru |trans-title=NFTs in gaming: regulatory issues, player anger, and developers' hasty decisions}}</ref> Both ''[[SlashFilm]]'' and ''[[GameSpot]]'' described the incident as plagiarism;<ref name="Meenan-2023"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/intergalactic-actor-talks-about-clashing-with-neil-druckmann-and-wanting-to-be-like-george-clooney/1100-6536163/ |website=[[GameSpot]] |title=Intergalactic Actor Talks About Clashing With Neil Druckmann And Wanting To Be Like George Clooney |first=Eddie |last=Makuch |date=November 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251117065130/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/intergalactic-actor-talks-about-clashing-with-neil-druckmann-and-wanting-to-be-like-george-clooney/1100-6536163/ |archive-date=November 17, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Devin Meenan referred to the partnership with Voiceverse as "one of Baker's less reputable roles", writing that "nobody's perfect."<ref name="Meenan-2023">{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1230802/troy-baker-thought-hed-have-a-much-smaller-role-in-hbos-the-last-of-us/ |title=Troy Baker Thought He'd Have A Much Smaller Role In HBO's The Last Of Us |first=Devin |last=Meenan |date=March 16, 2023 |access-date=October 19, 2025 |website=[[SlashFilm]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250908192533/https://www.slashfilm.com/1230802/troy-baker-thought-hed-have-a-much-smaller-role-in-hbos-the-last-of-us/ |archive-date=September 8, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The affair became an exemplar of the gaming community's broader rejection of NFTs. ''[[The Verge]]'' characterized the backlash with the subheading "His fans chose hate," writing that "not even Troy Baker, one of the most beloved voice actors in gaming, could get away with an NFT project,"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/22917126/nfts-crypto-gamers-music-fans-fandoms |title=Why gamers hate crypto, and music fans don't |first=Casey |last=Newton |date=February 4, 2022 |access-date=January 11, 2026 |website=[[The Verge]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221125071032/https://www.theverge.com/22917126/nfts-crypto-gamers-music-fans-fandoms|archive-date=November 25, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> and multiple news websites—including ''[[TheGamer]]'',<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thegamer.com/team17-scraps-nfts/ |title=Team17 Scraps MetaWorms NFT Project After Backlash From Developers And Fans |first=Joshua |last=Robertson |date=February 1, 2022 |access-date=January 11, 2026 |website=[[TheGamer]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211141848/https://www.thegamer.com/team17-scraps-nfts/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 11, 2022}}</ref> ''[[Digital Trends]]'',<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/canceled-gaming-nft-2022-2021/ |title=Every canceled video game NFT project (so far) |first=Tomas |last=Franzese |date=April 6, 2022 |access-date=January 11, 2026 |website=[[Digital Trends]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210201741/https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/canceled-gaming-nft-2022-2021/|archive-date=February 10, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Platformer (newsletter)|Platformer]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.platformer.news/why-gamers-hate-crypto-and-music/|title=Why gamers hate crypto, and music fans don't|first=Casey|last=Newton|author-link=Casey Newton|date=February 3, 2022|access-date=April 29, 2026|website=[[Platformer (newsletter)|Platformer]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260207193329/https://www.platformer.news/why-gamers-hate-crypto-and-music/|archive-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref> and ''[[PC Gamer]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/good-job-internet-you-bullied-nfts-out-of-mainstream-games/ |title=Good job, internet: You bullied NFTs out of mainstream games |first=Tyler |last=Wilde |date=January 2, 2023 |access-date=January 11, 2026 |website=[[PC Gamer]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121112248/https://www.pcgamer.com/good-job-internet-you-bullied-nfts-out-of-mainstream-games/|url-status=live |archive-date=January 21, 2023}}</ref>—grouped Baker's cancelled partnership alongside other failed gaming NFT projects.

''Plagiarism Today'''s Jonathan Bailey wrote that the incident was one of the earliest instances of "AI plagiariz[ing] AI" and commented that it presaged later [[artificial intelligence controversies|AI-related controversies]], such as [[OpenAI]]'s accusations that [[DeepSeek]] had [[Knowledge distillation|"distilled" their models]]. Bailey distinguished 15's case from corporate disputes, emphasizing that 15 was a solo developer who insisted on non-commercial use and that Voiceverse had directly used the 15.ai service rather than even attempting to distill the model.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bailey |first=Jonathan |date=November 17, 2025 |title=A Retrospective on the Voiceverse Plagiarism Scandal |url=https://www.plagiarismtoday.com/2025/11/17/a-retrospective-on-the-voiceverse-plagiarism-scandal/ |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=Plagiarism Today |archive-date=November 17, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251117211633/https://www.plagiarismtoday.com/2025/11/17/a-retrospective-on-the-voiceverse-plagiarism-scandal/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In January 2026, ''[[Eurogamer]]'' referenced the scandal in regards to Baker's comments about [[generative AI]], writing that his Voiceverse partnership had resulted in "fierce backlash" as a result of his "provocative marketing".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/actor-troy-baker-believes-ai-could-be-a-good-thing |title="We don't need to demonise it" - actor Troy Baker believes gen-AI could drive people to seek out "authentic" experiences |first=Robert |last=Purchese |date=January 6, 2026 |access-date=January 9, 2026 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> ''Hyperlific'' cited the plagiarism episode as an example of how voice-cloning technology could move from research use to commercial products and legal controversy.<ref>{{cite web |last=Editorial Team |date=March 19, 2026 |title=VoiceSynthetix Doesn't Exist, But the War Over Shinji Ikari's Voice Is Already Here|url=https://www.hyperlific.com/articles/voicesynthetix-doesnt-exist-but-the-war-over-shinji-ikaris-voice-is-already-here/|website=Hyperlific |access-date=July 1, 2026}}</ref>
